sources.notes: Every client below was tested on 2026-11-17 with a real request to /matters (latest matter) and a title search for 'eminent domain'/'condemnation'. No key needed for these clients. Max 1000 rows per request ($top/$skip). Other useful endpoints: /bodies, /events?$filter=EventDate ge datetime'..', /events/{id}/eventitems, /matters/{id}/attachments (PDF links), /matters/{id}/texts/{textId} (full text), /matters/{id}/histories. Place names are in the free text only - no geometry. 'active': false means the client answers but its newest matter is old (city left Legistar or stopped publishing). Not usable without a token: nyc and phila (HTTP 403, token required). Not on Legistar API (HTTP 500 'not set up'): Houston, Chicago (own eLMS API, see separate source), Los Angeles city, San Diego city, Indianapolis, Atlanta (current), Tucson, Las Vegas, Memphis, Omaha, Raleigh, Tampa, Tulsa, Honolulu among others tested.

summary: Checked 2026-11-17. Every source listed under sources was fetched live and real records read. Coverage: (1) City/county capital programs with GIS: Charlotte, Dallas, Raleigh, Durham, Virginia Beach, Norfolk, Nashville, Chattanooga, Seattle, Kirkland, Carlsbad, Fresno, LA County, San Antonio, Austin (watershed + light rail), Travis, Montgomery (TX), Harris Pct 4 and Harris County Flood Control, Hidalgo drainage district, Aurora and Denver CO, Mesa and Tucson AZ, Fairfax and Prince William VA, Montgomery MD, DC, NYC (three feeds), Boston, Detroit and GLWA, Cleveland NEORSD, St. Louis MSD, Kansas City, Minneapolis, New Orleans, Miami-Dade, Orange and Hillsborough FL, Fulton GA, Pittsburgh, Broken Arrow OK. (2) Legistar: 177 working client slugs verified with real requests (156 active), across 32 states, plus Chicago's own eLMS API. (3) Transit: LA Metro (including a parcel-level acquisitions layer), Valley Metro, Austin Transit Partnership, Charlotte CATS, Chicago RTA, MTA, COTA, Fairfax BRT, California High-Speed Rail, Atlanta Beltline. (4) Transmission/pipelines: TVA siting projects, OPPD, California CEC, a national third-party planned-transmission layer (Our Grid Future), SPP project list, EIA gas pipeline projects, Minnesota per-docket siting layers, Texas eminent-domain entity registry. HIFLD is verified but has almost no proposed lines. (5) Flood control, schools: Harris County FCD, Oklahoma state flood plan, LA County, St. Louis MSD; school programs for Wake County, Charlotte-Mecklenburg, NYC SCA and Connecticut. Not covered: no usable feed found for the cities of Los Angeles, Houston, Phoenix, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Indianapolis, Columbus, Jacksonville, Fort Worth, El Paso, Memphis, Oklahoma City, Las Vegas, Baltimore, Milwaukee, Albuquerque, Sacramento, Atlanta, Omaha, Tampa, Honolulu (searched ArcGIS Online and Socrata; they may have layers on their own servers that the catalog search did not surface). PJM, MISO, ERCOT, CAISO, NYISO and ISO-NE lists could not be verified as machine-readable; state utility-commission dockets have no APIs; no airport or port capital-project GIS found. Several servers (San Jose, Portland, Bexar, Baltimore County, Sioux Falls) timed out from this network and are listed as unverified. States with no source at all besides the national layers: AK, DE, ID, IN, ME, NH, SC, VT, WV. States with only Legistar clients (no project layer): HI, NV, NJ, OR, RI, UT, WI.
